question: A training manager is setting up a project so that every chat produces course outlines in the department's standard format. Which sequence of steps is correct?
options: A) Write the project instructions; refine the wording; define the audience and format; test with a real request.
B) Define the audience and format; write the project instructions; test with a real request; refine the wording.
C) Refine the wording; test with a real request; write the project instructions; define the audience and format.
D) Test with a real request; define the audience and format; refine the wording; write the project instructions.
correct_answers: B) Define the audience and format; write the project instructions; test with a real request; refine the wording.
explanations: Refining before the standard is defined means editing wording with no agreed target to edit towards.
Correct. Agree the standard, encode it as durable direction, try it on real work, then tighten what missed.
Nothing exists to refine at the start, and the format is agreed only after everything is already built.
Testing before any instructions exist tells you nothing about whether the instructions work.
